notes: Main disagreements: (1) modality in the framework report (vt-3), where coder A coded 'We ...'/'would benefit' statements as informs and coder B as should/must; resolved to informs because they are principles or plans, not rules. (2) policy type for near neighbours (P107 vs P04, P83 vs P66, P39 vs P69, P115 vs P63, P65 vs P05); resolved by the type definitions and what the sentence says. (3) unit_stance neutral vs encourage/permit on benefit statements and tool names; resolved to neutral when no instruction is given. (4) document stance for the College of Engineering page (A permit, B delegates); resolved to delegates. (5) coder B sometimes merged two rules into one unit (vt-3 verification plus disclosure; vt-4 ethical use plus modeling); kept as separate units. Coder B-only units in the honor-code page about general integrity training, a syllabus honor-code section and 'ignorance of the rules' were dropped as not about AI; B-only survey statistics and a duplicate principle in the framework were dropped; B's tier-detail unit duplicated the risk-tier rule. Alignment was by anchor position, with a few pairs matched by hand when the greedy match crossed two adjacent passages. Agreement shares are over matched units.
